subquestions.text_open:
9.1 Pyrrole (1) and pyridine (2) are two common nitrogen-containing aromatic rings with different reactivities.
9.1.1 Using resonance structures, determine the nucleophilic sites of pyrrole in aromatic electrophilic substitution. Give the SMILES of the major resonance structures of pyrrole.
9.1.2 Pyridine can be oxidized by H_2O_2 to **3**. Compare the nucleophilicities of **2** and **3**, and explain your answer.

9.2 A literature report describes a Lewis-acid-controlled electrophilic substitution between indole and triphenyl-1,3,5-triazinane.
9.2.1 Without a Lewis acid, a short sequence gives final product C; the first step is a thermal pericyclic reaction. Write the SMILES structures of the two key intermediates and product C.

text_images.description: A ('C12=CC=CC=C1C=CN2') and B ('N1(C2=CC=CC=C2)CN(C3=CC=CC=C3)CN(C4=CC=CC=C4)C1') react in DCE at 80℃ for 24h to give C (C_15H_14N_2).

subquestions.text_open: 9.2.2 In the presence of a Lewis acid, C undergoes Lewis-acid-catalyzed fragmentation and rearrangement to give product D. D and C have the same molecular formula. Write the SMILES of D.

text_images.description: A ('C12=CC=CC=C1C=CN2') and B ('N1(C2=CC=CC=C2)CN(C3=CC=CC=C3)CN(C4=CC=CC=C4)C1') react under Eu(OTf)_3 in DCE at 60℃ for 1h to give D (88%) and E.

subquestions.text_open: 9.2.3 In the presence of a Lewis acid, the reaction also produces a tetracyclic by-product E containing 2 five-membered rings and 2 six-membered rings. Write the SMILES of E.

9.4 A literature report describes an NHC-catalyzed synthesis of 2-pyrones. Interestingly, replacing the ketone substrate with an ester gives a fused-ring product with a different skeleton.
9.4.1 The first step in both reactions is activation of substrate F by the NHC. Write the SMILES of the activated intermediate, including the complete N-heterocyclic carbene structure.

text_images.description: F ('O=C(OC(C)=O)C#CC1=C2C(C=CC=C2)=CC=C1OC') and G ('[R]C(CC1=NC2=CC=CC=C2S1)=O') react under 'CC(C)(C)[C@H]1COCC2=NN(C3=C(C)C=C(C)C=C3C)[C]N21' (10 mol%), base, and solvent. Here R = Ph or R = OEt.

subquestions.text_open: 9.4.3 For R = Ph, write the SMILES structures of the product and the other 2 intermediates besides the answer to 9.4.1. NHC substituents may be represented by R, and stereochemistry is not required. The product is known to contain 5 six-membered rings.
9.4.4 Write the SMILES structure of the product when R = OEt; stereochemistry is not required. The product is known to contain 4 six-membered rings.
9.4.5 Determine whether the products of the preceding reactions are chiral.
